title: EFFINGHAM SHOOTING
full_story:
The Effingham Police Department and the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office requested the Illinois State Police (ISP) Division of Criminal Investigation Zone 8 to investigate a shooting incident at St. John’s Lutheran Church on Jefferson Avenue in Effingham.

On Sunday, at approximately 9:27 am, St. John’s Lutheran Church security contacted Effingham Police Department to report a suspicious vehicle and suspicious man inside the church wishing to speak with the pastor, no church service were occurring at the time.  The Effingham Police Department and the Effingham County Sheriff’s Office responded to the church and located the man a short time later.  The suspicious vehicle was reported stolen out of Marion County.  Officers from both agencies attempted to restrain the man.  During the struggle, the man produced a firearm, which discharged, and the man was struck.  The man was taken to a local hospital and later transported by helicopter to a regional hospital with life-threatening injuries.  No one else was injured in this incident.

The Marion County Sheriff’s Department says the vehicle had been stolen in Kinmundy at 8:55 Sunday morning.

This was an isolated incident and there is no known threat to the community at this time.

This is an active investigation, and no additional information is available at this time.

title: LOG CABIN BREAK IN
full_story:

title: STROKE RURAL GOLD RECOGNITION
full_story:
Fairfield Memorial Hospital received the American Heart Association’s Get With The Guidelines – Stroke Rural Gold Recognition Award, recognizing the hospital’s commitment to delivering high-quality, evidence-based stroke care to patients in rural communities.

People living in rural communities face significant health disparities. According to the American Heart Association, rural residents live an average of three years fewer than their urban counterparts, have a 40% higher likelihood of developing heart disease, and face a 30% greater risk of dying from a stroke.  Fairfield Memorial Hospital is committed to helping change those outcomes by ensuring patients receive timely, guideline-directed stroke care close to home.

Stroke is the fourth leading cause of death and a leading cause of long-term disability in the United States, according to the American Heart Association’s 2026 Heart Disease and Stroke Statistics Report.  A stroke occurs when blood flow to the brain is interrupted by either a blood clot or a ruptured blood vessel, depriving brain tissue of oxygen.  Rapid recognition and treatment are essential to improving survival, reducing disability, and increasing the likelihood of recovery.

The American Heart Association established the Get With The Guidelines – Stroke Rural Recognition program to honor rural hospitals that consistently provide high-quality stroke care based on nationally recognized clinical guidelines.  Award recipients demonstrate excellence in critical performance measures including timely stroke evaluation, brain imaging, emergency medical services communication, dysphagia screening, intravenous thrombolytic therapy when appropriate, stroke specialist consultation, documentation of symptom onset, and efficient transfer protocols when advanced care is needed.

The recognition reflects Fairfield Memorial Hospital’s ongoing commitment to clinical excellence and continuous quality improvement, ensuring patients throughout southeastern Illinois have access to lifesaving stroke care when every minute matters.

title: JULY BLOOD DRIVES
full_story:
ImpactLife will have a blood drive at the Clay County Hospital on Thursday, from 10 am to 1 pm.  To schedule an appointment at this drive go to https://login.bloodcenter.org/donor/schedules/drive_schedule/144076

The American Red Cross is also making an urgent call for blood donors to book an appointment to give now to ensure hospitals stay ready to help patients without delay.

There will be a blood drive Friday, July 10th from 1 to 5 pm at the Clay County Health Department.  All donors who donate blood during this drive will get a American Red Cross Looney Tunes T-shirt.  Then there will be a Blood Drive at the Flora Oddfellows Lodge on Friday July 24th from 1 to 5 pm.  Donors at this drive will get a Fandango Movie Reward by email.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  You can make an appointment to donate at Red Cross Blood Drives by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).  Save time with RapidPass.  Complete your pre-donation reading and health history at RedCrossBlood.org/RapidPass or with the Blood Donor App before your appointment.

title: OCC MASSAGE THERAPY SIGN UP
full_story:
Olney Central College’s Massage Therapy Program is accepting new students for Fall 2026.

Designed with busy adults in mind, the program offers convenient evening classes that allow students to pursue a rewarding new career without putting life on hold.  Best of all, the certificate can be completed in just one year.

While enrolled, students gain the skills needed to work in the wellness field of massage therapy, mastering professional massage techniques through hands-on classroom instruction and clinical experience. The program’s clinical opportunities, which are open to the public, provide students with valuable practice working with a variety of clients in a real-world setting.

Olney Central College is recognized as a National Certification Board for Therapeutic Massage & Bodywork (NCBTMB) Assigned School.  This designation confirms that OCC’s Massage Therapy Program meets the high standards of excellence established by the NCBTMB.  It also ensures that after successfully completing state licensure requirements, graduates are eligible to pursue NCBTMB board certification; the highest credential available in the massage therapy profession.

Enrollment is limited.  To reserve a spot, apply by July 15th at www.iecc.edu/apply.

title: HEART AND KIDNEY DRUG RECALL
full_story:
The Food and Drug Administration says nearly one million bottles of heart and kidney medication have been recalled nationally.  California-based Amgen, Inc. voluntarily recalled the bottles of Corlanor and Sensipar tablets after “unexpected foreign matter” was found in a sample of one of the identified lots.

According to the recall notice, 934,577 bottles of Corlanor, known by its generic name ivabradine, have been recalled because they contain “foreign substance” on the tablets.  Corlanor is a heart failure medication, and the bottles impacted are the 5mg, 14-tablet bottles.

Corlanor was approved by the FDA in 2015 and reduced the risk for hospitalization from worsening heart failure.

The 7.5mg, 60-count bottles of the same medication are also under recall for “presence of foreign substance.”  The number of bottles impacted are unknown, according to the notice.

Over 9,500 bottles of Sensipar, known for by its generic name cinacalcet, have been recalled for deviation of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP).  CGMP are a set of regulations by the FDA that establish standards that manufacturers must meet to be considered safe.

Sensipar is prescribed to patients with chronic kidney disease and those who have high levels of calcium in the blood related to parathyroid gland conditions.

The California State Board of Pharmacy said in an alert that hazard assessments have found it doesn’t present a clinical risk to patients and overall patient safety risk is low.  The tablets were distributed between October 28th, 2021 and December 30th, 2025.
